FloodMask: Flood Extent from Radar, With
Honest Uncertainty
PROBLEM STATEMENT
Clouds often hide floods from optical satellites, so radar is used instead. Radar water maps can still
confuse flood water with permanent water, radar shadow and urban areas. Build a mapper that
outputs flood extent alongside a per-pixel "unsure" layer, rather than forcing a confident label
everywhere.
DESCRIPTION / IMPLEMENTATION
-
Data: Use Sen1Floods11, which includes Sentinel-1 imagery and 446 hand-labelled chips drawn
from 11 flood events. Organizers must publish the permitted training data and reserve a genuinely
organizer-controlled event/case set with labels withheld for final scoring; a publicly downloadable
label set alone is not a hidden test.
-
Implementation: Predict flood water, permanent water and not-water. Compare against the
dataset Otsu-threshold radar baseline; weakly labelled data may be used if its noise is documented.
-
Evaluation: Hold out whole flood events, not random chips. Report flood-class F1 and IoU versus
Otsu, calibration, error-versus-coverage when the model abstains, and failures in urban areas,
radar shadow and permanent water.
-
Stretch: Mask aligned Sentinel-2 chips to simulate cloud and show where radar adds information.
Explain mismatches and alignment limitations rather than treating every difference as a model
error.
DELIVERABLES
-
Minimum prototype: A map viewer with radar chip, flood prediction, per-pixel uncertainty layer,
difference from the Otsu baseline and a per-event score table.
-
A repeatable pipeline and report containing hidden-event scores, calibration and
error-versus-coverage results.
-
A short limitations note explaining the small hand-labelled set, event-level holdout and weak-label
noise.

OpenForce: Measuring the Effort to
Open Everyday Packaging
PROBLEM STATEMENT
"Hard to open" is a feeling until someone measures it. Build an instrumented rig that
measures the peak force or torque and effort profile needed to open packaging, so
opening aids can be compared with repeatable measurements rather than impressions.
DESCRIPTION / IMPLEMENTATION
-
Implementation: Build a rig with a load cell or torque sensor, amplifier and
microcontroller. Calibrate it against known masses or known torque, and log
timestamped effort curves.
-
Test at least three types of empty packaging with and without an opening aid, keeping
the mounting and test procedure consistent. The no-aid result is the baseline.
-
Evaluation: Report calibration error, repeatability across repeated trials, drift over time
and measurement uncertainty. Conduct a blind comparison of two aid designs using
organizer-selected samples or test conditions; disclose the test protocol after scoring.
-
Stretch: Add a second measurement axis, such as grip force versus twist torque. Use
empty packaging only; make no clinical claims. Human-subject trials are optional and
require informed consent.
DELIVERABLES
-
Minimum prototype: A working rig with live readout, sensor calibration record and
timestamped force/torque curves.
-
A results table comparing at least three packaging types with and without an aid,
including repeated-trial error bars and a blind aid comparison.
-
A short test protocol and limitations note describing measurement range, uncertainty
and sources of drift.

BreathGate: Breathing-Rate Estimation
That Abstains When the Signal Is Bad
PROBLEM STATEMENT
Breathing rate can be estimated from a pulse-sensor signal, but noise and motion can make
estimates unreliable. Build an estimator that reports a rate only when it has enough signal
evidence and otherwise says "unreliable". It must not diagnose or recommend treatment.
DESCRIPTION / IMPLEMENTATION
-
Data: Use the BIDMC dataset of 53 eight-minute recordings containing photoplethysmography
(PPG), impedance respiration and ECG signals with reference respiratory rates. The two manual
breath annotations differ slightly; report their spread as part of the reference uncertainty.
-
Implementation: Add signal-quality gating and a breathing-rate estimator; compare it with a
simple spectral-peak baseline. Organizers must use a subject-level split and withhold
evaluation references in a locked scoring set; publicly downloadable labels alone cannot be
described as hidden test labels.
-
Evaluation: Split by subject, not by windows. Report error in breaths per minute against
coverage, errors on accepted and rejected windows, and results after injecting motion noise
and signal dropouts.
-
Stretch: Run on a microcontroller-class device and report latency and memory use. Clearly
label the result as a signal-processing prototype, not a medical device.
DELIVERABLES
-
Minimum prototype: A signal viewer showing the waveform, estimated rate, confidence or
quality indicator, and an explicit abstain flag.
-
An error-versus-coverage curve and a report comparing the spectral-peak baseline with the
proposed estimator on held-out subjects.
-
A failure-case summary for motion noise, dropouts and disagreement between reference
annotations.

BUILD TYPE  |  SOFTWARE
TraceBack: Reconstructing an Intrusion
Timeline from Raw Logs
PROBLEM STATEMENT
After an incident, analysts face thousands of unlabelled events from many machines. Build a
tool that proposes a timeline of attacker steps, links each step to the log evidence behind it, and
marks weak links as "uncertain". The tool works on logs only and must not include exploit code.
DESCRIPTION / IMPLEMENTATION
-
Data: Start with OTRF Security Datasets (formerly Mordor), which contain recorded events
from simulated adversary techniques alongside benign activity. Because public traces may be
too small for multi-host evaluation, organizers must also prepare a reproducible multi-host
scenario with benign noise and keep its ground-truth attack-step list hidden until scoring.
-
Implementation: Correlate events across hosts and users into candidate attack steps. Every
proposed step must link to supporting log evidence, and weak causal links must be explicitly
marked uncertain.
-
Evaluation: Compare with the baseline that sorts events by time and groups them by host.
Score recall of true attack steps, precision of causal links, false links caused by benign bursts,
and robustness to clock skew and late-arriving logs.
-
Stretch: Add a counterfactual panel showing which events would change a proposed link and
what benign explanation could fit the same pattern.
DELIVERABLES
-
Minimum prototype: A timeline view, evidence drill-down, uncertain-link flags and a score
report against the organizer-held scenario.
-
A repeatable log parser/correlation pipeline and a baseline comparison with attack-step recall,
causal-link precision and false-link counts.
-
A failure-case summary covering clock skew, delayed events and benign activity; no live
network access or exploit code.

VentRate: Estimating Room Ventilation
Rate from CO2, With Uncertainty
PROBLEM STATEMENT
A CO2 reading is not a ventilation rate. Build a sensor node that estimates how quickly a
room’s air is being replaced, reports an uncertainty range, and indicates when the estimate
should not be trusted.
DESCRIPTION / IMPLEMENTATION
-
Implementation: Build a CO2 sensor node with a microcontroller. State whether the sensor
measures CO2 directly or infers it, and estimate air-change rate from a decay curve. Decay
testing requires an unoccupied space and approximately constant ventilation during the test.
-
Evaluation: Test at least three ventilation conditions against a documented reference, such
as a fan with measured flow or defined door/window states. Compare the estimate against
a plain ppm-threshold baseline.
-
Evaluate sensitivity to sensor placement and non-uniform mixing; report
reference-versus-estimate error and an uncertainty range. Organizers should reserve one
condition or placement for a blind final test and keep its reference values out of the
development materials.
-
Stretch: Add a second sensor to quantify how non-uniform mixing changes the estimate. Do
not present a ppm threshold alone as an air-change measurement.
DELIVERABLES
-
Minimum prototype: A working sensor node with live CO2 readings and a ventilation-rate
estimate plus an explicit uncertainty or unreliable state.
-
A reference-versus-estimate table across at least three conditions, including the blind
condition, and a comparison with the ppm-threshold baseline.
-
A documented limits page covering sensor type, sensor placement, well-mixed-air
assumptions and situations in which no reliable estimate should be shown.
